week1.head: Bills 36, Texans 31 (at Houston, Sep 13)
week1.text: Josh Allen 20/29, 334 yards, no turnovers; game-winning 96-yard drive. New WR D.J. Moore 100 yards and a TD; TE Dalton Kincaid a career-high 130 yards. The defense, in coordinator Jim Leonhard's debut, let Houston convert nine third/fourth downs and allowed 31; CB Christian Benford struggled against Nico Collins. Joe Brady's first win as head coach.

week1.head: Lions 31, Saints 30 in OT (Detroit, Sep 13)
week1.text: Jared Goff 26/39, 206 yards, 2 TD, 0 INT. Jahmyr Gibbs 29 carries, 156 yards, 2 TD (team 165 rushing). Amon-Ra St. Brown 10 catches, 2 TD including the OT winner. Detroit won the turnover battle 3–1 and still needed a failed Saints two-point try to survive: New Orleans put up 469 yards, mostly after halftime. Played a full overtime on the short week.

injuries.read: Two days in, the story is unchanged and a little worse for Detroit: left guard and a tackle have not practised, the starting center is limited, the starting center from camp is on IR, and now a starting corner (D.J. Reed) is limited — against Allen, Moore and Kincaid, with Joseph and Branch already out. Buffalo's new worry is its own secondary: Cole Bishop, the safety Buscaglia thinks could be the defense's next star, did not practise Tuesday. Nothing here is a surprise to the market — the line moved 1.5 toward Buffalo before any of it was official — but a Bishop or Moore 'out' on Wednesday would move it again.

weather.text: National Weather Service (issued Mon Sep 14): showers likely in the morning and early afternoon Thursday, then mostly cloudy; kickoff-time conditions about 61–65°F, 30% chance of a shower, wind light and variable. Not a weather game unless the forecast changes.

venue.text: First game ever in the new Highmark Stadium. The Bills tested the new grass field on Tuesday (Sal Maiorana); Joe Brady on the opener: not trying to put on a show, 'trying to put on a clinic'. Nobody has a home-field number for the building; last season the Bills were 4–5 against the spread at home.

voices.who: Lions beat writers on X (Tue Sep 15)
voices.take: Nolan Bianchi (Detroit News) posted the Tuesday estimated report: no practice again for Mahogany and Blake Miller, D.J. Reed limited (foot), Scruggs limited, Izien fine. Justin Rogers: of the Lions' defensive starters from the 48–42 game in 2024, only Jack Campbell and Alim McNeill will start this week — this is a very different Detroit defense. Dave Birkett: Campbell says Mahogany's injury isn't serious long-term but Thursday is 'tough'.

voices.who: Bills beat writers on X (Tue Sep 15)
voices.take: Joe Buscaglia (The Athletic), Matt Parrino, Katherine Fitzgerald: Cole Bishop did not practise (leg sleeve), T.J. Sanders sent home ill, Ty Johnson back out there, D.J. Moore left early then returned. Parrino: Jim Leonhard saw 'a lot of ugly' between the two Rousseau strip-sacks vs Houston. Maiorana: the Bills' defense 'needs to get some things fixed' against a much better Lions offense.

Action Network logged the early move as Lions +3.5 → +4.5. Warren Sharp's Week 1 table has Detroit second in the league in yards before contact per rush (+2.55) — the Gibbs run game is real. No sharp-side call on this game from the accounts I could read; the rest of the X search results were ticket resellers and parlay touts.
Lions +4.5 and Over 53.5 — Buffalo's defense just allowed 31 to Houston; both offenses combined for 67 in Week 1; short-week fatigue is an overblown narrative.

voices.who: r/sportsbook daily thread (Sep 15, three relevant comments out of ~36)
voices.take: One bettor thinks a 102.5 Lions team-rushing prop is mispriced after 165 yards last week; another is laddering Allen passing yards because Detroit's secondary is, in his words, Swiss cheese; a third has Bills on a parlay. No consensus, thin thread.
r/detroitlions: relief after surviving the Saints' second-half comeback — 'a win is a win'. r/buffalobills: celebrating Joe Brady's first win and D.J. Moore as the new WR1. Mood, not information.
